kept.q: A man of mass 60 kg climbs a vertical ladder of height 4 m in 8 seconds. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, calculate the average power he develops.
kept.explanation: Work done = mgh = 60 x 10 x 4 = 2400 J. Power = work/time = 2400/8 = 300 W.
kept.pidgin: Work wey e do = mgh = 60 x 10 x 4 = 2400 J. Power = work divide by time = 2400/8 = 300 W.

kept.q: A trailer of mass 1500 kg moving at 20 m/s is brought to rest by a constant braking force acting over a distance of 50 m. Using the work-energy theorem, calculate the magnitude of the braking force.
kept.explanation: By the work-energy theorem, F x d = (1/2)mv^2. So F = (0.5 x 1500 x 20^2)/50 = 300000/50 = 6000 N.
kept.pidgin: Work-energy theorem say F x d = (1/2)mv^2. So F = (0.5 x 1500 x 20^2)/50 = 300000/50 = 6000 N.

kept.q: A small ball of mass 0.5 kg is released from rest at the top of a smooth frictionless incline of vertical height 1.25 m. Using the principle of conservation of energy, find the speed of the ball when it reaches the bottom of the incline. Take g = 10 m/s^2.
kept.explanation: Since the incline is smooth, loss in PE equals gain in KE: mgh = (1/2)mv^2, so v = sqrt(2gh) = sqrt(2 x 10 x 1.25) = sqrt(25) = 5 m/s.
kept.pidgin: Since the incline no get friction, the PE wey e lose turn to KE: mgh = (1/2)mv^2, so v = sqrt(2gh) = sqrt(2 x 10 x 1.25) = sqrt(25) = 5 m/s.

kept.q: A pump raises water from a well at a rate of 2 cubic metres per minute to a height of 15 m. If the density of water is 1000 kg/m^3, g = 10 m/s^2, and the pump works at an efficiency of 80%, calculate the power input required to operate the pump.
kept.explanation: Mass flow rate = 2 x 1000/60 = 33.33 kg/s. Useful output power = mgh per second = 33.33 x 10 x 15 = 5000 W. Since efficiency = output/input, input power = 5000/0.8 = 6250 W.
kept.pidgin: Mass wey dey flow per second = 2 x 1000/60 = 33.33 kg/s. The output power = mgh per second = 33.33 x 10 x 15 = 5000 W. Since efficiency = output/input, input power = 5000/0.8 = 6250 W.
